name: Grand Canyon
description: A breathtaking gorge over 400 km long and 1.6 km deep, carved over millions of years by the Colorado River.

name: Statue of Liberty
description: A colossal copper statue gifted by France in 1886, standing on Liberty Island as an enduring symbol of freedom.

name: Golden Gate Bridge
description: An iconic 2.7 km suspension bridge spanning the Golden Gate strait at the entrance to San Francisco Bay, completed in 1937.

name: Space Needle
description: A futuristic observation tower built for the 1962 World's Fair in Seattle, standing 184 m tall with a revolving restaurant.

name: Hollywood Sign
description: A landmark sign on Mount Lee in the Santa Monica Mountains overlooking Los Angeles, originally erected in 1923 as an advertisement.

name: Everglades National Park
description: A vast subtropical wilderness of wetlands, mangroves, and sawgrass prairies in southern Florida, home to alligators, manatees, and Florida panthers.

name: Diamond Head
description: A dormant volcanic tuff cone on O'ahu, its distinctive silhouette visible across Honolulu, offering panoramic views from its 232-meter summit.

name: Gateway Arch
description: A gleaming 192-meter stainless steel arch in St. Louis, the tallest man-made monument in the Western Hemisphere, symbolizing America's westward expansion.

name: Hoover Dam
description: A massive concrete arch-gravity dam on the Nevada-Arizona border built between 1931 and 1936, creating Lake Mead, the largest US reservoir by volume.

name: Rocky Mountain National Park
description: A stunning alpine park in northern Colorado with jagged peaks, glacial valleys, and tundra above 3,000 m, including 14 summits over 4,200 m.

name: Mount Rushmore
description: A massive granite sculpture in the Black Hills depicting the 60-foot faces of four US presidents, completed between 1927 and 1941.

name: The Alamo
description: A former Spanish mission in San Antonio that was the site of a famous 1836 battle during the Texas Revolution.

name: Liberty Bell
description: An iconic cracked bronze bell in Philadelphia, originally rung to summon lawmakers to legislative sessions, now a symbol of American independence.

name: Niagara Falls
description: A group of three massive waterfalls on the border between New York and Ontario, Canada, drawing millions of visitors each year.

name: Yellowstone
description: America's first national park, established in 1872, famous for its geothermal features including the Old Faithful geyser and vivid hot springs.

name: Arches National Park
description: A high-desert park in eastern Utah containing over 2,000 natural sandstone arches, including the iconic Delicate Arch, shaped by millions of years of erosion.

name: Kennedy Space Center
description: NASA's primary launch facility on Merritt Island, from which all Apollo moon missions launched and which continues to support crewed spaceflight today.

name: Willis Tower
description: A 442-meter skyscraper in Chicago, the tallest building in the Western Hemisphere from 1973 to 1998, featuring glass-floored observation boxes on the 103rd floor.

name: Graceland
description: The Memphis mansion of Elvis Presley, one of the most visited private homes in America, preserved as a museum to the King of Rock and Roll.

name: French Quarter
description: The oldest neighborhood in New Orleans, known for its French and Spanish Creole architecture, jazz music, and the famous Mardi Gras celebrations.

name: Cape Hatteras Lighthouse
description: The tallest brick lighthouse in the United States at 63 meters, standing on the Outer Banks to warn ships of the treacherous Diamond Shoals.

name: Shenandoah National Park
description: A mountain park stretching along the Blue Ridge Mountains in Virginia, famous for Skyline Drive, ancient Appalachian forests, and sweeping valley views.

name: Mammoth Cave
description: The world's longest known cave system beneath the hills of central Kentucky, with over 660 km of surveyed passageways and UNESCO World Heritage status.

name: Stone Mountain
description: The largest exposed granite monolith in the world near Atlanta, featuring a massive bas-relief carving of Confederate leaders and panoramic views from its summit.

name: White Sands National Park
description: The world's largest gypsum dune field in southern New Mexico, where brilliant white sand dunes rise up to 18 meters across 710 km² of surreal desert landscape.

name: Independence Hall
description: The historic Philadelphia building where both the Declaration of Independence and the US Constitution were debated and adopted.

name: Alcatraz Island
description: A former federal penitentiary on a rocky island in San Francisco Bay that once held notorious criminals and is now a popular museum.

name: Crater Lake
description: The deepest lake in the United States, formed in the caldera of a collapsed volcano and known for its extraordinary blue color and clarity.

name: Denali
description: The highest peak in North America at 6,190 m, located in central Alaska and surrounded by a vast national park of glaciers and tundra.

name: Monument Valley
description: A vast red-rock landscape on the Arizona-Utah border featuring iconic sandstone buttes rising up to 300 m from the desert floor.

name: Monticello
description: Thomas Jefferson's neoclassical plantation home in Charlottesville, designed by the third president himself and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

name: Theodore Roosevelt National Park
description: A rugged badlands park in western North Dakota featuring dramatically eroded buttes, petrified forests, and roaming bison herds.

name: Acadia National Park
description: The first national park established east of the Mississippi, encompassing granite peaks, rocky coastline, and pristine forests on Mount Desert Island off the Maine coast.

name: Mackinac Island
description: A historic island in Lake Huron where motor vehicles have been banned since 1898, known for Victorian architecture, horse-drawn carriages, and the landmark Grand Hotel.

name: Carlsbad Caverns
description: A vast limestone cave network in the Guadalupe Mountains, home to the largest cave chamber in North America and nightly mass flights of up to 400,000 bats.
